script: My dad rebuilt the same Minecraft house forty times because he could not remember he had already built it. He was fifty six. Early onset, the doctors called it, which is a very clean phrase for something that is not clean at all. He had played with me since I was seven. That was our thing. Not sports, not fishing. A world we started in 2011 that we never deleted. When he began forgetting things in the real world, he still knew that world perfectly. He knew where every chest was. He knew which path went to the mine without looking. My mother said it was the only hour of the day he did not seem afraid. Then he started rebuilding the house. The same house, in the same clearing, with the same spruce wood, over and over. He would log in, walk to that spot, and start again, and he did not understand why the ground was already flat. I did not tell him. I logged in every night and I helped him build it, and when he logged off I would quietly take the extra house down so the clearing would be empty for him the next day. Forty times. I have the screenshots. He always put the door on the wrong side, the same wrong side, every single time. Toward the water instead of the path. I never corrected it once. The last one we built was in March. He got about halfway, to the second wall, and then he stopped moving. He sat there in the game for a long minute. Then he typed in the chat, not out loud, in the chat, he typed, I know I have done this before. I did not know what to say to that. So I typed back, yes, thirty nine times. And he typed, was it good. And I said it was the best one. He logged off. He did not log in again after that. The world is still there. The half built house is still there, second wall unfinished, door already placed on the wrong side.
